title: 19 Myths Of Managing Difficult Students
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin opens by describing a "mountain of misinformation" that circulates among teachers about how to handle difficult students, calling it confusing, contradictory, and ultimately ineffective because it treats symptoms rather than root causes. He lists nineteen widely repeated pieces of advice he considers myths, including giving extra attention, offering choices, pep-talks, reward systems, behavior contracts, and reflection forms, framing all of them as band-aids that fail to change behavior in any lasting way. He argues the very premise that managing difficult students must be a stressful daily struggle is itself a myth. Once teachers understand what these students truly need, he writes, the work becomes far less difficult. He reframes difficult students as kids in need of direction, restored dignity, and reactivated intrinsic motivation rather than kids who must be managed through bribery or appeasement.
points: Common classroom-management advice for difficult students is described as a 'band-aid' that fails to address the root cause of misbehavior.
Nineteen specific practices are named as myths, including extra attention, choices, pep-talks, rewards, behavior contracts, and reflection forms.
The belief that difficult students must be appeased, coddled, or bribed is itself identified as a harmful myth.
Difficult students are reframed as kids needing direction and restored dignity, not kids who require special management tricks.
Understanding what these students truly need removes much of the stress associated with managing them.
